cohort: The study analyzed variables from the Live Births Information System (Sinasc) covering 19 Regional Health Coordinations in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
finding: Higher maternal education, presence of a partner, and adequate prenatal consultations reduced vaginal delivery frequency, while low schooling was associated with prematurity and low birth weight, and low prenatal coverage correlated positively with Apgar score > 7 and negatively with adequate birth weight.
mod_finding: Higher maternal education, the presence of a partner, and an adequate number of prenatal consultations were associated with a reduced frequency of vaginal delivery, and the overall proportion of cesarean section was 62%.
birth_weight: low birth weight, adequate birth weight
